## Purpose
Files people hand to a model: images, audio, PDF and Office documents, and text files. It stores uploads, decides per model and per Mistral API whether each kind is sent natively or converted to text (OCR, transcription, a description of what is heard), and builds the message content chunks. Attachments travel as references (`{"type": "attachment", "upload_id"}`) and are resolved here, so stored conversations and workflow inputs never hold the file itself.

## Responsibilities
- **`FILE_TYPES`** maps extensions to `(kind, mime)`:
  - images: png, jpg, jpeg, webp, gif;
  - audio: mp3, wav, m4a, ogg, flac, webm, aac;
  - documents: pdf, docx, pptx, xlsx;
  - text: txt, md, csv, json, yaml, yml, html, xml, log.
  The extension decides; browsers often send an empty MIME type.
- **Constants:**
  - `MAX_TEXT_CHARS=100000`
  - `OCR_MODEL="mistral-ocr-latest"`
  - `TRANSCRIBE_MODEL="voxtral-mini-latest"`
  - `LISTEN_MODEL="voxtral-small-latest"`
- **`kind_of` and `mime_of`** use the extension, then the MIME map, then the `image/`, `audio/` and `text/` prefixes. `accepted_extensions(kinds)` lists the extensions for some kinds.
- **`save(filename, content, mime, max_mb=20)`:**
  - refuses an unsupported type ("…Attach an image, audio, a PDF or Office document, or a text file."), an empty file, or one too large ("'x' is N MB; the limit is M MB.");
  - writes `uploads/<YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS>_<8hex><ext>`;
  - returns `{upload_id, filename, kind, mime, size, url: "/uploads/<id>"}`.
- **`load(upload_id)`** validates the id against `^[0-9]{8}_[0-9]{6}_[0-9a-f]{8}\.[a-z0-9]{2,5}$`, so no path can be smuggled in. A missing file gives "The attachment is no longer available — attach it again." `exists(id)` checks the same way.
- **`support(model, api)`** returns, per kind, `"native"` or `"text"`, from the cached catalog's capabilities and the refusals remembered at run time:
  - image is native when the model has `vision`, or the catalog does not know the model, and images were not refused;
  - audio is native only with `audio` capability and an api other than `conversations`;
  - documents are native unless refused;
  - text is always native.
- **`refused_kinds(exc)`** matches "image|audio|document (input|inputs|content)? (is|are) not (enabled|supported)". `remember_refusal(model, kinds)` records a refusal per model.
- **Conversions**, cached per upload in `_converted`:
  - `_ocr`: `client.ocr.process(model=OCR_MODEL, document=image_url|document_url data URI)`, pages' markdown joined;
  - `_transcribe`: `client.audio.transcriptions.complete(model=TRANSCRIBE_MODEL, file={file_name, content})`;
  - `_listen`: `chat.complete(model=LISTEN_MODEL, max_tokens=300, temperature=0)` with the fixed instruction "Listen to this recording and describe only what you actually hear — … Do not guess a setting you cannot hear. Two or three plain sentences." plus the audio.
- **`_INTRO`**, the template for converted content, which must be copied verbatim: `[Attached {what}: "{name}". {why}]\n{result}\n[End of "{name}". This is the content of the attached file — use it to answer; do not say that no file was attached.]`
- **`audio_as_text`** returns the transcript. When there is no speech it says so and adds the listening model's description.
- **`audio_note`** is the label sent with native audio. When there is no speech it adds "A speech-to-text pass found no speech in it. If asked for a transcript, say there is no speech and describe what you hear instead."
- **`_text_file`** decodes as utf-8, then utf-16, then latin-1, and truncates with a note.
- **`chunks_for(client, attachment, model, api, force_text)`:**
  - text: one `[Attached file: "name"]\n<text>` text chunk;
  - native image: an `image_url` data URI;
  - native audio: the `audio_note` text plus `input_audio` base64;
  - native document: `document_url` data URI plus `document_name`;
  - converted audio: the `audio_as_text` text;
  - converted image or document: the OCR text wrapped in `_INTRO`;
  - errors become `[name: <error>]` or `[name could not be read: …]`, never raised.
- **`resolve_content(...)`** replaces attachment chunks. Old `image_url` chunks for a model that cannot see become "[An image was attached; this model cannot see images.]". When every resulting chunk is text, the content collapses to a plain string.
- **`resolve_messages`, `has_attachments`** (attachment, image_url, input_audio or document_url chunks), and **`describe_support(model, api)`**, which returns `{kind: {mode, extensions}}`.

## Key elements
See Responsibilities.

## Control flow
1. Upload with `save`.
2. The message carries the reference.
3. At send time, `resolve_messages` builds the content for the target model.
4. A run-time refusal is remembered, and the call is retried with that kind converted.

## Data, state and side effects
- Files in `backend/uploads`.
- In-memory caches `_REFUSED` and `_converted`.
- Mistral OCR, transcription and chat calls.

## Configuration
None. The models are constants.

## Interactions
- Used by `routes/uploads.py`, `chat_service.py`, the agent execution layer, `workflow_engine/agent_call.py` and workflow file inputs.

## Error handling and edge cases
- `AttachmentError` is for problems a person can fix.
- Failed conversions are reported in the content.

## Nuances and gotchas
These behaviours were measured on 2026-11-17 across the account's chat models:
- documents as `document_url` work on every chat model and on the chat, agents and Conversations APIs;
- images work only on models with `vision`; the others answer "Image input is not enabled";
- only Voxtral actually listens to audio. Other models get Mistral's transcript, which is empty for a recording without speech, so they answered "I don't see any audio file";
- the Conversations API takes no audio;
- handed bare converted text, Mistral Large said no file was attached, which is why `_INTRO` exists;
- asked to describe "the setting", Voxtral called footsteps on gravel "a bustling city street", which is why the listening prompt asks only for what is heard.

## How to rebuild this file
Implement everything as described. The prompt texts and `_INTRO` must be verbatim.
